views.name: Coins · joint premises
views.title: The challenge has three joint premises.
views.intro: Permission, assumed unawareness, and the supplied bridge feed one inference. The factual reply attacks C2 directly.
views.note: C8 is a conditional editorial conclusion, not a new source claim. Compare Code to see the numbered premises and uses: [1, 2, 3]. No undercut is asserted.

views.name: River · two inference steps
views.title: Comparison, then temporal qualification.
views.intro: The first step states the compared categories. The second jointly uses that intermediate conclusion and Rashi’s awareness-before-pickup qualification.
views.note: R9 is a supplied intermediate statement. R6 is the existing qualified conclusion, reused with identical meaning. The Gemara’s refutation and ruling are recorded, not computed.

views.name: Opening · Abaye / Rava premises
views.title: Where does each legal conclusion come from?
views.intro: Abaye points to present unawareness; Rava points to despair expected upon awareness. The supplied bridges state how each reason is taken to bear on yeush now.
views.note: O9 and O10 are editorial normative bridges, not Hebrew quotations or independently established premises. O1–O3 remain isolated scope notes: these inferences concern ordinary unmarked loss only. O5 → O7 records the opposed positions, not an undercut.
